observations.summary: The moved #[cfg] attribute: reject_private_name was inserted between the existing #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] and fn lift_capture, so the attribute now gates reject_private_name and lift_capture lost it (it was macOS-only at HEAD). mod private_access is not gated by target (only #[allow(dead_code)]), so on Linux lift_capture would now compile as unused code with the warning suppressed. No macOS behavior change: Z1 restores the attribute and the owner test and probes still pass with no warnings. Not checked by a Linux build here (only the macOS standard library is installed). Restore #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] on lift_capture.

The shared check's backslash and NUL branches are pinned only by reviewer probes: the owner test uses four of the six refused shapes (Y3 survives); adding 'a\\b' and 'a\\0b' to the loop would pin the whole condition.

From r1: as_file widens RetainedDirectory (design note); the observation-to-creation window analysed as acceptable; the full security suite needs a custody-safe TMPDIR; unused From impls and nested WorkFailure.

limits: This macOS development host (APFS) only; the functions are macOS-only; as_file and now lift_capture also compile on Linux, not built here.
